comment: The sole error was assuming wider C would outperform deeper A. At this tiny SGD rate, width is not a reliable proxy for useful progress; cloned-layer depth and initialization can affect near-initial CE. Their causal contributions remain unmeasured. Backtesting found deeper/narrower transformers winning 2/2 matched-recipe history comparisons, both from q_b8b3c5. Lab analogues at SGD .001 without momentum favored depth32×4 over width64×1 on 4/4 datasets, but these are not exact A/C controls. Other low-rate plain-SGD history comparisons reversed that preference, so no universal depth rule survives. K1019 helped identify weak progress; I overextended K1068’s width tendency despite its scope warning. K1017 and K1012 correctly cautioned against this complete shape ordering.

def build_transition(

    alpha: float = 1.0,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    rng = np.random.default_rng(table_seed)
    logits = rng.standard_normal((vocab_size, vocab_size)) * alpha
    logits -= logits.max(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    probs = np.exp(logits)
